name: Adversary-Operated AI Agent
description: The attacker runs AI agents of their own — a single agent, a swarm, or an orchestrator with sub-agents, often on self-hosted or refusal-stripped models — to carry out reconnaissance, exploitation, credential chaining, collection and persistence against targets with little human direction per step. Offensive agent consoles, autonomous penetration-testing frameworks, offensive forks of coding agents, and the persona, scope, doctrine and skill files that drive them are its artefacts.
differs: The agent belongs to the attacker: nothing in the target's AI is compromised, so detection relies on the agent's behaviour and infrastructure — machine-paced request bursts, agent tool user agents, exposed operator consoles, persona, scope and skill files. When the target's own agent is steered into harmful actions, that is Agentic Tool Misuse (T3.001); an agent placed inside the target's environment and tasked remotely is AI Agent Implant & Command Channel (T9.005). Producing malicious content with a model, without an agent acting on targets, stays in the harmful-use registry (R009, R013, R014).
